denomProfiles/malankara-orthodox/tagline: Kerala's autocephalous St Thomas church, led by the Catholicos of the East at Kottayam.
denomProfiles/malankara-orthodox/coreDoc: Oriental Orthodox (Miaphysite) faith, accepting the councils of Nicaea, Constantinople and Ephesus.
Traces its origin to the apostle Thomas's mission to India, traditionally dated AD 52.
Holds that the Catholicate of the East, established in Malankara in 1912, makes it an autocephalous church.
Seven sacraments; the Eucharist is the true body and blood of Christ.
Governed by the 1934 Constitution, which the Supreme Court of India upheld in 1995 and 2017.
denomProfiles/malankara-orthodox/focuses: Defending its autocephaly and the 1934 Constitution in its long dispute with the Patriarch's faction.
Education, hospitals and charitable institutions in Kerala.
Ecumenism: a founding member of the World Council of Churches (1948).
Pastoral care of a large Malayali diaspora in the Gulf, Europe and North America.
denomProfiles/malankara-orthodox/practic: West Syriac liturgy (Holy Qurbana of St James) celebrated mainly in Malayalam, with Syriac and English.
Veneration of St Gregorios of Parumala, canonised in 1947 and the object of a major annual pilgrimage.
Lenten and other fasts, including the 25-day pre-Christmas fast and the three-day Nineveh fast.
Married priests; bishops (metropolitans) chosen from celibate clergy and elected by the Malankara Association.
Parish life centred on the palli (church) with festivals (perunnal) for patron saints.
denomProfiles/malankara-orthodox/influen: Formed in 1930 when Mar Ivanios and others entered communion with Rome.
Theologian Paulos Mar Gregorios served as a president of the World Council of Churches (1983–1991).
Emerged from a 19th-century reform party within the Malankara church.
denomProfiles/malankara-orthodox/keyFigu: Malankara Metropolitan who led the move to establish the Catholicate
Bishop and first canonised saint of the church
Catholicos of the East and Malankara Metropolitan since 2021
denomProfiles/malankara-orthodox/inIndia: Based at Devalokam, Kottayam, the church is concentrated in central Kerala, with dioceses across India; its long dispute with the Jacobite faction over churches and property turned on the Supreme Court's 2017 judgment for the 1934 Constitution.
denomProfiles/eritrean-orthodox-tewahedo: Eritrea's Ge'ez-rite Orthodox church, autocephalous since 1993, under heavy state pressure.
Tewahedo ('made one') Christology: Christ's divinity and humanity united in one nature, as in the Coptic and Ethiopian churches.
Accepts the councils of Nicaea, Constantinople and Ephesus and rejects Chalcedon.
The broad Ethiopian-tradition canon of 81 books, including Enoch and Jubilees.
Seven sacraments and the real change of bread and wine in the Qiddase (liturgy).
Strong veneration of the Virgin Mary (Kidane Mehret, 'Covenant of Mercy') and the saints.
Building an independent national church after Eritrean independence (1993).
Monastic tradition, notably the ancient monastery of Debre Bizen.
Ge'ez liturgy, chant (zema attributed to Yared) and church schools.
Surviving government control, including the 2006 removal of Patriarch Antonios.
Liturgy in Ge'ez with Tigrinya; the tabot (altar tablet) consecrates each church.
Around 180 fasting days a year for the devout, including Wednesdays and Fridays.
Timket (Epiphany) processions with the tabot, and Meskel (Finding of the Cross).
Distinctive observances shared with Ethiopia: Saturday as well as Sunday sabbath, circumcision and dietary rules.
Debteras (cantors) sing the services with drums and sistra.
Eritrean diaspora churches
Parishes in Europe and North America, some of which reject the government-installed hierarchy.
Debre Bizen and Eritrean monasticism
A spiritual centre for Orthodox in Eritrea and Tigray.
Abune Philipos (patriarch 1998–2002)
First patriarch of the autocephalous church
Abune Antonios (1927–2022)
Third patriarch, deposed in 2006 and held under house arrest until his death
Yared
Patron of liturgical chant
denomProfiles/malankara-jacobite-syrian/: Kerala's St Thomas Christians who remain loyal to the Syriac Orthodox Patriarch of Antioch.
Oriental Orthodox (Miaphysite) faith identical to that of the Syriac Orthodox Church.
The Patriarch of Antioch is supreme head; the Catholicos of India is a regional primate under him.
Apostolic origin from St Thomas, combined with the Antiochene succession received after 1665.
Seven sacraments, the Divine Liturgy of St James and the intercession of Mary and the saints.
Loyalty to the throne of Antioch, symbolised by patriarchal visits and relics in Kerala.
Retaining parishes and identity after Supreme Court rulings (1995, 2017) favoured the Malankara Orthodox.
Social institutions, schools and colleges in Ernakulam and central Kerala.
Pilgrimage to shrines such as Manarcad St Mary's and the tomb of St Baselios Yeldho at Kothamangalam.
Holy Qurbana in Malayalam and Syriac following the West Syriac rite.
The eight-day Lent of St Mary (1–8 September) at Manarcad and other Marian churches.
Commemoration of Patriarch Ignatius Elias III, who died at Manjinikkara in 1932.
Married parish priests (kathanars) and celibate bishops.
Malayali diaspora parishes
Dioceses and parishes in the Gulf, Europe and North America under the Patriarch.
Indian Syriac identity
Keeps alive the Antiochene link in Kerala's church life.
Baselios Paulose II (1914–1996)
Installed as Catholicos in 1975 by Patriarch Yaqub III
Baselios Thomas I (1929–2024)
Catholicos of India 2002–2024, who led the church through the litigation
Ignatius Elias III
Patriarch who died in Kerala in 1932, venerated at Manjinikkara

Centred at Puthencruz near Ernakulam, it is one of the two main successors of the Malankara Syrian Church in Kerala; after the 2017 judgment it lost many contested churches and built or acquired new ones.
denomProfiles/mar-thoma-syrian/tagline: Reformed Oriental church: St Thomas heritage, Syriac liturgy, evangelical theology.
denomProfiles/mar-thoma-syrian/coreDoctr: Scripture is the supreme rule of faith; the 19th-century reform removed practices judged unbiblical.
Rejects prayers to the saints, prayers for the dead and the doctrine that the Eucharist is a sacrifice for the dead.
Retains episcopal order, infant baptism and a reformed West Syriac liturgy.
Accepts the Nicene Creed and the ancient creedal faith of the Church.
Salvation by grace through faith, with strong emphasis on personal conversion and holiness.
denomProfiles/mar-thoma-syrian/focuses/0: Evangelism through the Mar Thoma Evangelistic Association (1888) and ashrams across India.
denomProfiles/mar-thoma-syrian/focuses/1: Bible study, preaching and Sunday schools in Malayalam.
denomProfiles/mar-thoma-syrian/focuses/2: Ecumenism: in full communion with the Church of South India, the Church of North India and the Anglican Communion.
denomProfiles/mar-thoma-syrian/focuses/3: Social service: schools, colleges, hospitals and work among the poor.
denomProfiles/mar-thoma-syrian/practices: Holy Qurbana in Malayalam, a revision of the Liturgy of St James translated by the reformers.
The Maramon Convention, held each February on the sands of the Pamba river since 1895.
Infant baptism and confirmation; married clergy and celibate bishops.
Strong lay participation through parish assemblies and the Prathinidhi Mandalam (representative council).
denomProfiles/mar-thoma-syrian/influence: St Thomas Evangelical Church of India
Partner in full communion and in the Communion of Churches in India.
Its ashrams and evangelists work among non-Christian communities across India.
denomProfiles/mar-thoma-syrian/inIndia: Headquartered at Tiruvalla, Kerala, it has dioceses across India and in the diaspora; its Maramon Convention is among the largest annual Christian gatherings in Asia.
denomProfiles/armenian-catholicosate-cil: The Armenian Church's second catholicosate, rebuilt at Antelias, Lebanon, after the genocide.
The faith of the Armenian Apostolic Church: Miaphysite Christology and the first three ecumenical councils.
One church with two catholicosates; Cilicia is administratively independent of Holy Etchmiadzin.
Seven sacraments; the Eucharist is celebrated with unleavened bread and unmixed wine.
Veneration of the Virgin Mary, Gregory the Illuminator and the Armenian saints and martyrs.
Rebuilding Armenian church life in the Middle East after the 1915 genocide and 1921 expulsion from Cilicia.
Diaspora identity: language, schools and seminary education at Antelias and Bikfaya.
Ecumenism: Catholicos Aram I moderated the WCC Central Committee (1991–2006).
Commemoration of the genocide and support for Armenians in Syria and Lebanon.
Divine Liturgy of the Armenian rite (Badarak) in Classical Armenian.
Christmas and Epiphany celebrated together on 6 January.
Blessing of holy muron (chrism), traditionally every seven years.
Married parish priests and celibate vardapets (doctor-monks) from whom bishops are chosen.
Its Tehran diocese ordained a woman to the diaconate in 2017, reviving an ancient order.
Armenian diaspora dioceses
Jurisdiction in Lebanon, Syria, Cyprus, Iran, the Gulf, Greece and parts of North America.
Oriental Orthodox ecumenism
Joint initiatives with the Coptic and Syriac churches in the Middle East Council of Churches.
Gregory the Illuminator
Founder of the Armenian Church
Nerses IV Shnorhali (c. 1102–1173)
Catholicos, poet and theologian
Sahak II Khabayan (catholicos 1902–1939)
Led the see from Sis into exile and resettled it at Antelias in 1930
Karekin II Sarkissian (catholicos 1977–1995)
Later Catholicos Karekin I of Etchmiadzin
Aram I Keshishian
Catholicos since 1995
denomProfiles/church-of-the-east/tagline: The Persian church of the Silk Road, which reached from Mesopotamia to China and India.
denomProfiles/church-of-the-east/coreDoc: Dyophysite Christology in the Antiochene tradition: two natures and two qnome in the one person of Christ.
Honours Theodore of Mopsuestia as 'the Interpreter' and rejected the Council of Ephesus (431).
Declared its independence from western bishops at the Synod of Dadisho (424).
Sacramental life including the 'holy leaven' (malka), regarded as a sacrament alongside baptism and Eucharist.
Mary honoured as 'Mother of Christ' rather than 'Mother of God' (Theotokos).
denomProfiles/church-of-the-east/focuses: Missionary expansion across Central Asia, China (from 635), Mongolia and India.
Schools of theology and medicine, notably Nisibis and Gundeshapur.
Translation of Greek philosophy and science into Syriac and Arabic under the Abbasids.
Survival as a minority under Zoroastrian, Muslim and Mongol rulers.
denomProfiles/church-of-the-east/practic: Liturgy of Addai and Mari, one of the oldest anaphoras in use.
East Syriac chant, office and calendar.
Veneration of the cross rather than images in many periods.
Married clergy, including bishops in early centuries; later bishops were monastic.
Monasticism reformed by Abraham of Kashkar (6th century).
denomProfiles/church-of-the-east/influen: Formed from members who entered union with Rome from 1553.
St Thomas Christians who received East Syriac bishops for centuries.
The Xi'an stele (781) records the 'Luminous Religion' brought by Alopen.
denomProfiles/church-of-the-east/keyFigu: Led the mission to Tang China in 635
Organised missions and debated the caliph al-Mahdi
Ascetic writer read across all Christian traditions
Envoy from Mongol China to Europe in 1287–88
denomProfiles/church-of-the-east/inIndia: The St Thomas Christians of Malabar received bishops and the East Syriac liturgy from the Church of the East until the Portuguese imposed Latin rule (Synod of Diamper, 1599).
